narrative:
The bank’s decision to deny your loan was based on an analysis of your financial profile, which suggested a higher likelihood of difficulty repaying the loan. The model estimated that there was nearly a 50% chance you might struggle to meet the repayment terms—a threshold the bank uses to make these decisions. While this isn’t a guarantee of failure, it’s a signal that the bank needs to be cautious.

Three key factors stood out in this assessment. First, the bank noticed that you don’t have an active checking account with a regular balance, which is common among approved applicants. While many borrowers also fall into this category, the model treats it as a sign of limited financial stability, especially when combined with other factors.

Second, the purpose of your loan—a new car—played a role in the decision. Applicants seeking loans for cars, whether new or used, tend to have higher default rates compared to those borrowing for essentials like furniture or education. The bank likely saw this as a riskier choice, particularly given the amount you requested, which was significantly lower than the average loan approved. While smaller loans might seem less risky on paper, the model may have interpreted this as a sign of needing quick access to funds without a clear plan for long-term repayment.

Finally, having a co-applicant on your loan added to the uncertainty. While this might seem like a safety net, the model may have viewed it as a red flag, suggesting that your financial situation alone wasn’t strong enough to secure the loan without additional support. Most approved applicants don’t have co-applicants, which could imply the bank sees this as a sign of weaker individual financial standing.

To improve your chances in the future, focus on building a stronger financial foundation. Opening a checking account with regular deposits and saving more—even small amounts—could help demonstrate stability. If you’re considering another loan, explore options with lower risk, like those for education or home improvements, and aim to borrow closer to the average amount. Finally, reducing reliance on co-applicants by strengthening your own financial profile will make your application more compelling.

The target variable is whether the applicant will be a bad credit risk.

Protected attributes sex, age and foreign_worker were not used to make the machine prediction.

A SHAP value tells you how much a feature influenced the prediction (larger absolute value means a stronger influence) and its direction: positive pushes toward bad credit risk, negative toward good credit risk. Below are the top 3 features by absolute SHAP value.
